analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY uptrend is intact (+3.7% vs SMA50, slope positive). The macro backdrop supports holding quality longs, but does NOT compel forcing new entries.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• A (+14.5%): Strong performer, Agilent thesis intact — quality instruments business benefiting from biopharma capex. No action needed.
• AMP (+5.9%): Ameriprise compounding steadily, financial services tailwind. Hold.
• LMT (+6.4%): Defense spend structural tailwind. Thesis intact. Hold.
• MCO (+2.9%): Moody's is a tollbooth business. Modest gain but thesis fully intact. Hold.
• TEL (+0.5%): Essentially flat since entry. Still in the candidate list as UPTREND (basing), SMA50 slope nearly flat (+0.5%), sitting -0.9% below SMA200. No confirmed thesis break — revenue growing +13.8%, strong FCF — but the setup is the weakest in the book. Not a sell trigger yet; watch for a close below $207 (prior base support) as a thesis-break signal.

CRITICAL CAPACITY CONSTRAINT: Gross deployment is 94% of equity with only ~$1,029 of headroom before hitting the 95% cap. There is literally no room to add a meaningful new position without selling an existing one. Any forced 'buy' at this size would be a rounding error with no real impact — and would add transaction cost and complexity with zero portfolio benefit.

PERFORMANCE HONESTY CHECK: Profit factor is 0.55x (losses outpacing gains in dollar terms), Sortino -0.81. This is a clear warning sign. The right response to a sub-1.0 profit factor is NOT to trade more aggressively — it is to hold the good positions you have (all showing gains), wait for the book to breathe, and only act when a genuinely asymmetric setup AND the capacity to size it properly coincide. Neither condition is met today.

DECISION: Zero new trades. Cash is the correct posture for new capital. Existing positions are all in-the-money and thesis-intact. The discipline of doing nothing when capacity and conviction alignment are absent is itself alpha-preserving behavior.
